what_this_is: whether the restricted-route disclosure is a property of the published answer or of the traversal order

control.what_this_is: the positive control: a four-node construction whose disclosure IS ambiguous, so the instrument's ability to report a moved flag is demonstrated rather than assumed

what_the_real_graph_says: the flag moved on 0 of 69,078 flagged nodes across three relabellings. Exact bit-level cost ties between differently flagged routes do not occur on this graph, so the disclosure is well defined here
why_this_still_matters: the ambiguity is a property of the MODEL, not of this graph. It is latent and it would surface the moment costs are quantised -- integer seconds, a rounded penalty, a deliberately coarse cost unit -- because quantisation manufactures exact ties. Anyone proposing to make the cost integral has to rerun this with --graph first
and_what_it_does_not_claim: that the flag is correct. It says the flag does not depend on traversal order on this graph. Whether the route it describes is the route a person can walk is the walked audit's question and remains unanswered
